To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) HLA class I ligands of the inhibitory NK cell receptor KIR2DL2 and KIR2DL3 are associated with a better clinical outcome of HCV-related HCC after curative treatment; 2) KIR2DL1 and KIR3DL1 are associated with worse clinical outcome of HCC after cura- tive treatment; 3) the HLA class I alleles Cw7, Bw4, Bw4/27,
the HLA class I and killer immunoglobulin -like receptor (KIR) genes are important outcome predictors in patients with HCV -related hepatocellular cancer (HCC) after curative treatment.
the KIR/HLA system is a prognostic marker in patients undergoing curative treatment of HCV-related hepatocellular carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) genes and their HLA ligand genes in patients with HCV-related HCC.
the development of new imaging techniques for the detection of breast cancer and the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of breast cancer and other malignancies.
the study of the killer immunoglobin-like receptors and their ligands in the context of the immune system and its interaction with the human body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KIR gene family is a major factor in the outcome of the disease, and that the KIR genes are a major factor in determining the outcome of the infection.
the KIR/HLA system is involved in HCV pathogenesis and in the clinical course of the disease.
KIRs are important in the pathogenesis of HLA-associated diseases, but the role of the KIR-HLA system in the development of HCC is still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of HLA-Cw4 in patients with HCV-related HCC and KIR3DS1 in HCV-negative patients with HCC is associated with a poor clinical outcome.
the KIR/HLA system is a powerful predictor of the clinical outcome in HCV-related hepatocellular carcinoma.
the KIR2DL1 gene and its ligand HLA-C1 were associated with the development of HCV-related hepatocellular carcinoma, while the KIR2DS4 gene was associated with better survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KIR2DL2 and KIR2DL3 are not involved in HLA-Bw4-mediated NK cell inhibition, which is in contrast to previous studies.
